(a) The pairing, `judgesByConversion` and `printAppliedEdits`.
- Join key: `judgesByConversion` reads `todo.conversionIds ?? []` for every todo and nothing else — no read of `surface`, `reason`, `replacement` or `acceptanceCriteria`, no regex, no `includes` over prose. On `main`, `applyMetaMigrations` builds each todo as `{ ...s, toMajor: step.toMajor }` (`chain.ts`), so the entry's declared field reaches the printer unchanged, and `MigrationTodo extends SemanticMigration` types it. Declared links only. RIGHT.

[]` prints nothing under a conversion no entry names. The guard `if (result.applied.length > 0)` is unchanged. Pin 3 asserts the no-review-line case over the dashboard conversion and compares every `    • ` line against `appliedLines(result)`, in order. RIGHT.
- One review line per contiguous run: `chain.ts` replays, per step, `for (const conversionId of step.conversionIds)` one `conversion.apply(current, cb)` at a time, and the callback pushes every edit of that call before the next conversion starts, so a conversion's edits are contiguous within its hop. Across hops: `conversions.test.ts:535` pins conversion ids unique, `migrations.test.ts` pins that a step's conversion ids all have `toMajor === major` (a graduated conversion belongs to its own major's step only), and step 18's list is derived from `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR[18]`, so no id is replayed in two hops. "Contiguous by construction" is true on `main`. And the printer does not depend on it: a split run would get its own review line, so the degenerate case loses nothing. The run counter resets on a conversion boundary, and the subject reads "the edit above" for one, "the N edits above" otherwise. RIGHT.
- Cross-hop: the join runs over the flat `result.todos` × `result.applied`, which hold only the hops the run crossed (`composeMigrationChain` filters `m > fromMajor && m <= toMajor`). So a review line can never name an entry of an uncrossed hop (it is not in `todos`), and cannot miss an entry it did cross whose conversion produced an edit in this run (both halves are in the flat arrays whatever hop made them). Pin 8 proves the earlier-hop direction on a real `--from 16` result by injecting an 18-entry → 17-conversion link (`action-execute-to-target`, `toMajor: 17`) and asserts `edit.toMajor` below `judge.toMajor`. Semantic observation, not a defect of this PR: a cross-hop link pairs only when both hops are crossed in one run — on a `--from 17` run the 17 conversion is not replayed, so the entry prints in ③ with no review line, correctly; on a `--from 16 --to 17` run the entry is not in the report at all. That is the data model (the entry belongs to its hop), and no cross-hop link is authored today. RIGHT.
